Thank you for the history; given the swelling in your right knee and the significant familial history, this suggests a genetic component like Hemophilia. Are you currently experiencing any bleeding from gums, nose, or after minor injuries like cuts or dental work?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 12.2 g/dL, Hematocrit: 36%, Leukocyte_count: 7,300/mm3, Platelet_count: 200,000/mm³, PT: 14.0 s, PTT: Not Reported (ACT: 52.0 s prolonged found in prior data, but specific PTT not in current request scope), Right_Knee_XRay: No fracture or dislocation noted (Ultrasound indicated hemarthrosis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; the normal platelet count and PT, combined with the prolonged ACT and ultrasound showing hemarthrosis, strongly suggest a coagulation factor deficiency rather than a platelet disorder. Have you ever noticed excessive bruising or bleeding after surgery or trauma in yourself or your family members?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency)
